name: Mushroomfolk
body:
Mushroomfolk are species of humanoid fungus who hail from the most remote of underground caverns. In their own language, spoken in voices that sounds like squishy, squeaky musical instruments, they call themselves the ooshoo.

As a society, they are reclusive and extremely cautious in their dealings with other peoples, and as such are rarely seen by any other than their immediate neighbors. Most individual mushroomfolk are diligent workers that single-mindedly spend their entire lives working for the colony, but they do have a sense of individualism—no matter how small—and occasionally even decide to become adventurers.

Physical

Mushroomfolk are stocky, humanoid-shaped plant creatures with bloated, spongy flesh. Their skin tones tend towards shades of tan and gray, but occasionally include dull shades of various pastels such as reds, pinks, and purples. Their heads are topped with a fungal cap, which is usually a darker shade of the same color as the rest of their flesh. They have no distinguishable neck, and their heads are barely separated from their bodies. Their faces are only notable as such by a pair of large eyes, as they have no mouths and no visible ears. They eat by standing on their food, usually while they sleep, and prefer their food slightly rotten to aid in digestion.

Young mushroomfolk are immobile, resembling toadstool mushrooms, but mature rapidly—reaching their equivalent of adolescence within a year. Once they reach this point, they begin to move about and work for the colony, and slowly grow to full size after four or five years. After this point, their aging is unpredictable: they grow as needed to fill roles missing in their colony.

Adult mushroomfolk typically live about two decades before showing any signs of age.

At this point they begin to slow physically, and after a few more decades they finally become immobile and begin to decay. A decaying mushroomfolk releases spores that grow into new mushroomfolk.

Social

Mushroomfolk are quick to listen, slow to talk, and even slower to act. Although they are willing to act without planning, they are much less willing to act without a firm grasp of their surroundings and situation.

Recklessness is unknown to them. Those who have adventured for some length of time will learn to act with less information if the situation forces them to, but a mushroomfolk straight from the colony is likely to be cautious to a fault.

Mushroomfolk, especially those removed from their colony, are hard workers, and prefer to finish an entire day’s work in one continuous action. When the day’s work is done their preferred form of recreation is a type of telepathically shared hallucination, 20 but without other mushroomfolk to share the experience with they are likely to attempt to join in whatever form of recreation is common among those hosting them.

Mushroomfolk consider most people to be their friends, and enjoy large gatherings.

Though loyal, they will not fight to help a friend unless to defend that friend. An enemy of a friend is not an enemy to a mushroomfolk, but someone who attacks that friend is.

Most mushroomfolk never leave their colony, but instead spend their life working.

However, though most never visit the outside world, they still prefer to keep track of events outside the colony. Colonies occasionally send scouts to explore the world and come back with stories; these scouts often join groups adventurers and spend most of their lives abroad before returning with what they know. Not all mushroomfolk adventurers are scouts— mushroomfolk have free will independent of their colony and on occasion get wanderlust. These individuals typically stay with their colony until a season where they are not needed, then strike off on their own.

Alignment And Religion

Most mushroomfolk are Lawful Neutral, prioritizing the needs of the colony over any individual desires they may have—although exceptions can be found.

Mushroomfolk primarily follow druidic religious practices, and indeed they are the primary practitioners of that faith throughout the subterranean realms.

Names

Some typical mushroomfolk names include the following (choose or roll 1d12): 1 Armalla, 2 Ayooli, 3 Bella, 4 Borta, 5 Choro, 6 Compia, 7 Geo, 8 Lucia, 9 Ooyae, 10 Pezi, 11 Postan, 12 Zomy

Standard Species Traits
Ability Score Modifiers You are durable and intuitive, but your fungal body is not built for strength or charm. Your ability score modifiers are +2 Con, +2 Wis, –2 Str, –4 Cha [mixed weakness]. (–2)
Size At character creation, choose either Medium or Small size. As a Medium creature, you have no bonuses or penalties due to size. As a Small creature, you have a +1 size bonus on attack rolls, a +1 size bonus to your Armor Class, a –1 size penalty to your CMB, and a +4 size bonus on Stealth checks; you must use smaller weapons than Medium creatures. As a Medium or Small creature, you occupy a space of 5 feet by 5 feet, and your reach is 5 feet. (0)
Type You are a Plant. (10)
Speed Your base speed is 30 feet. (0)
Languages You begin play speaking Ooshoo. If you have a high Intelligence score, you can choose from any of the following languages: Common, Sylvan, Treant, and Undercommon. (0)
Alternate Species Traits
Cave Dweller You gain a +1 bonus on Knowledge (dungeoneering) and Survival checks made underground. (1)
Darkvision You have darkvision to a range of 60 feet. (2)
Limited Plant Benefits Although you are a plant, you do not gain the standard immunities associated with creatures of the plant type. Instead, you gain a +2 species bonus on saving throws against mind-affecting effects, paralysis, poison, polymorph, sleep, and stunning effects—unless the effect specifies that it is effective against creatures of the plant type. (–5)
Limited Telepathy You are able to mentally communicate with any creature within 30 feet with whom you share a language. Otherwise, this ability is identical to the telepathy universal monster ability. (3)
Low-light Vision You can see twice as far as a human in starlight, moonlight, torchlight, and similar conditions of poor illumination. You retain the ability to distinguish color and detail under these conditions. (—)
Psychoactive Spores Once per day as a standard action, you can create a cloud around yourself with a radius of 5 feet for 1d4 rounds. Creatures who begin their turn within the cloud or who enter the cloud must attempt a Fortitude saving throw (DC 10 + 1/2 your character level + your Constitution modifier) or be confused (as the confusion spell) for 1 round. This is a mind-affecting poison effect. (2)
Total: 11 RP (advanced)
Alternate Species Traits
Bioluminescence Your skin radiates constant light, projecting dim light in a 5-ft. radius like a candle. This light is a color of your choice; once selected, this color does not change. You can suppress or resume this effect as a standard action. This trait replaces darkvision.
Forest Dweller Unlike many of your kin, you do not dwell underground but in the most secluded old-growth forests. You gain a +2 species bonus to Knowledge (nature) and Survival checks. This trait replaces cave dweller and darkvision.
Glitter Spores Once per day as a standard action, you can create a cloud of spores around yourself with a radius of 10 feet. This functions as glitterdust except that it is an extraordinary effect and must be centered on yourself. You are immune to your own glitter spores. This trait replaces psychoactive spores.
Paralytic Spores Once per day as a standard action, you can create a cloud around yourself with a radius of 5 feet for 1d4 rounds. Creatures who begin their turn within the cloud or who enter the cloud must attempt a Fortitude saving throw (DC 10 + 1/2 your character level + your Constitution modifier) or be slowed (as the slow spell) for 1 round. This is a poison effect. This trait replaces psychoactive spores.
Subterranean Stealth Your coloration and skill at blending in with natural stone formations make you difficult to spot underground. You gain a +4 species bonus to Stealth checks made in subterranean environments. This trait replaces cave dweller.
Toxic Spores A number of times per day equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum 1/day), you can envenom a weapon you wield with special spores your fungal body produces. Applying the toxin in this way is a swift action. This trait replaces psychoactive spores. Mushroomfolk Toxin: injury; save Fort DC 10 + 1/2 your Hit Dice + your Constitution modifier; frequency 1/round for 4 rounds; effect 1d3 Str; cure 1 save.
Feats
Extra Spores

You can use your spore defenses more than once per day.

Prerequisite(s): mushroomfolk, character level 3rd.

Benefit(s): You gain one additional use per day of your psychoactive spores species trait, or one additional use of whatever alternate species trait chosen you chose place of psychoactive spores.

Special: You can take this feat multiple times. Its effects stack.

Humongous Fungus

Your fibrous body grows to larger and stronger, even as you feel your reflexes begin to dull.

Prerequisite(s): Con 13, mushroomfolk, character level 5th.

Benefit(s): You permanently grow one size category, from Small to Medium or from Medium to Large. Your Strength increases by 2 and your Dexterity decreases by 2.

Special: If you began as size Small, you can take this feat twice—advancing first to from Small size to Medium size, and then from Medium size to Large.

Alternative Favored Class Bonuses
Alchemist Gain +1/4 additional use per day of your psychoactive spores species trait, or of whatever alternate species trait you selected in place of psychoactive spores.
Barbarian Add a +1/2 bonus to trap sense in forest or subterranean environments.
Cleric Add +1/2 to your channeled energy total when healing creatures of the animal, plant, and vermin types.
Druid Add a +1/2 bonus to your wild empathy or plant empathy checks.
Fighter Add +1 to your CMD when resisting a dirty trick or trip attempt.
Kineticist Add +1/3 point of damage to wood element blasts that deal damage.
Monk Add +1 to your CMD when resisting a grapple or trip attempt.
Occultist Gain a +1/3 bonus on all skill checks using occult skill unlocks.
Psychic Increase the total number of points in your phrenic pool by +1/3 point.
Ranger Add +1/4 to a single existing favored terrain bonus (maximum bonus +1 per favored terrain). You must be at least 3rd level to select this benefit.
Rogue Add a +1/2 bonus on Perception checks while in a forest or subterranean environment.
Sorcerer Add +1 spell known from the sorcerer spell list. This spell must be at least one level below the highest-level sorcerer spell you can cast.
Witch Add a +1/3 bonus on saving throws against mind-affecting effects and poison made by your familiar. If you ever replace your familiar, the new familiar gains these saving throw bonuses.
